newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged after supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged after supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat in early trading Thursday, after most of the week's new issues priced successfully earlier in the week.
"It's been very choppy over the last few sessions," one trader said. "One thing buoying the market is the fact that we have low supply and the deals seem to have gone pretty well."
The trader noted the Blue List of secondary market offerings had dropped to $1.2 billion Thursday.
New issues got most of the attention this week, including Wednesday's $500 million Chicago Board of Education issue and $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corp. deal.
The other large issue, a $932 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey deal, may still price Friday, according to a source familiar with the offering.
Thursday's early pricings included a $47 million Financing Authority for Resource Efficiency of California, tentatively priced by Bear, Stearns & Co. at a top yield of 5.92 percent in 2027.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract was off 1/32 at 112-19/32, while June T-bonds were up 1/32 at 107-24/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 155 ticks from 157 at the close Wednesday.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was unchanged at 94-10/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday are expected to total $460 million in 19 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $319 million in five sales, with a $154 million Virginia Public Building Authority deal through Craigie Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $141 million are on the schedule. A $44 million Milwaukee County, Wis., deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
